Our initial ask is a short technical demo to confirm Redwood's Dedicated sizing and a timeline for a pilot.

Can someone from your team do a 30–45 minute intake/demo next week? We're in PST. Time windows that work for us: Dec 10 10–11am, Dec 13 2–4pm. Also happy to take a brief intake questionnaire ahead of time — if you have a template.

Ben — thanks, picking Dec 13 2:30pm PST works for us. Confirmed.

Answers to your quick questions below so Karthik has context ahead of the call:
- Traffic profile: mostly idle; we see product-driven bursts when users trigger batch generation. Typical pattern is idle for minutes, then short bursts ~10–25s reaching 120–180 QPS. Planning for headroom to 200 QPS.
- Latency targets: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms (we know p95 will be higher for longer sequences).
- Models: evaluating open 13B variants (we'll be testing a 13B quantized float/4-bit setup).
- Tokens per request: ~60–90 tokens on average; some longer multi-turn interactions up to 300 tokens.
- Important: we need determinism for A/B parity vs our current internal model; we may request a canary rollout and fallback behavior.

Attached the profile (streamline_capacity_profile.xlsx). Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Olivia

Thanks for the context, Olivia — Karthik from Solutions Eng here. Quick technical notes before the call and items we'll cover so we can make the session productive:

1) Capacity/back-of-envelope sizing: given 150–200 QPS burst target with ~75 tokens, we'll walk through Dedicated pool sizing (GPU choices, concurrency per-GPU) and caching/batching knobs. Expect to discuss continuous batching vs low-latency mode.
2) Latency SLOs: p50 <120ms is achievable in many setups; p95 <350ms is reasonable depending on sequence length and quantization. We'll show benchmark numbers for 13B quantized variants and explain tradeoffs.
3) Loadtest/runbook: if you want, Redwood can help run a short pilot loadtest in a dedicated environment — we'll need a short runbook and approval.
4) Pre-call ask: please drop a sample prompt volume (tokens per minute) or a small csv of request size distribution if you have it — that speeds sizing.

I'll join today's 2:30pm PST and bring a short benchmark deck. If you want K8s/networking/topology visibility (VPC egress, firewall), mention it on the call.

—Karthik
